title: Oncall Psychological Safety & Handoff Checklist
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This checklist captures behavioral guardrails, concrete handoff steps, and tooling guidance for platform operators to preserve psychological safety during oncall shifts and incident handoffs. The goal is to reduce cognitive load, prevent blame, and ensure reliable context transfer so teams can make correct decisions under stress.

Audience
--------
- Platform operators (first- and second-line)
- Platform oncall leads
- Engineering managers and team leads who run rotations

Why this matters
----------------
- Oncall is high-cognitive-load work; poor handoffs increase time-to-restore and escalate stress.
- Psychological safety reduces fear of speaking up, which improves post-incident learning and reduces repeat errors.
- A short standardized handoff plus behavioral expectations prevents context loss during busy windows (deploys, high traffic) and multi-team incidents.

Principles (short)
------------------
- People > Pager: prioritize health and respectful communication over triaging every non-critical alert.
- Assume good intent: treat missing details as coordination gaps, not blame.
- Make implicit knowledge explicit: write what you would have wanted to know when you were in the middle of an incident.

Pre-shift checklist (what the incoming operator should do before taking the pager)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Review your upcoming 2-hour window on the platform-operator-dashboard; note any active experiments, deploy windows, or maintenance tasks.
2. Read the last 24h Handoff Note (see Handoff template below). If the outgoing operator attached a runbook ticket or incident ID, open it now.
3. Confirm PagerDuty assignment and communication channels (Slack: #platform-oncall, Incident Bridge URL).
4. Ensure you have access to the three quick tools: telemetry query UI, service-graph, and incident-tracker (local aliases: p-telemetry, p-graph, p-inc).
5. State a definite time to the outgoing operator for the swap (do not do asynchronous handoffs during active mitigation unless required).

During-shift behavioral expectations
-----------------------------------
- Communicate status concisely: short updates in #platform-oncall reduce redundancy (format: [SYSTEM] short-status — next-step — ETA).
- Use clarifying questions rather than assumptions. If you don’t understand a decision, ask in-bridge: "Can you confirm why we chose X vs fallback Y?"
- Declare escalation early: if an incident looks broad or crosses teams, tag sev2/3 and call the SRE lead.
- Pause and rest: if you’re fatigued, notify the outgoing or escalation contact and request a swap. Safety > completion.

Handoff pattern (structured template)
-------------------------------------
Always use the template below. If the handoff is verbal, paste this into the incident-tracker and Slack immediately after.

Handoff Title: [service-name] — brief status (e.g., "kv-prefix-cache: degraded, 15% error rate")
- Incident/Runbook ID: <ID or none>
- Current impact: (user-visible effects, customers affected)
- Last action taken: (what I did and when)
- Next required step (explicit, single-owner recommended): (e.g., "force-restart shard 4 via pctl; rollback prefetch experiment if errors persist")
- Open hypotheses (bullet list): (e.g., "1) prefetched KV writeback saturation; 2) kernel-level GPU memory fragmentation")
- Known mitigations and outcomes to date: (what worked/didn't)
- Data to watch (links): (telemetry query, dashboard panels, span IDs)
- Escalation contacts: (name + preferred channel)
- Confidences / TODOs: (explicit unknowns and blockers)

Example (one-line brief)
------------------------
kv-prefix-cache — degraded reads across us-west; rollback of prefetch-2 experiment pending; see runbook: p-inc-4912

Emergency swap criteria (when the incoming operator may request immediate takeover)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Outgoing operator is actively in another oncall-critical incident and cannot provide a coherent handoff.
- The outgoing operator reports fatigue, unclear mental state, or requests swap.
- There is new, high-severity customer impact that requires fresh context.
If criteria are met, perform an emergency swap and create an Incident Swap note in the incident-tracker with timestamp and reasons.

Communication language guide (phrases to use)
--------------------------------------------
- Use: "I’m unsure — can we slow down and confirm the last action?"
- Use: "I’m going to take a minute to reproduce this locally before escalating."
- Avoid: "That was dumb/obvious"; instead say: "We didn’t factor X into the experiment; let’s record it."

Post-handoff housekeeping (outgoing operator responsibilities)
-------------------------------------------------------------
- Attach telemetry snapshots and any terminal logs to the incident-tracker.
- Mark unresolved follow-ups in the incident-tracker and assign owners.
- Add a single-line summary to #platform-oncall and tag the next oncall.
- If you were the owner of a mitigation, note whether it should be rolled forward or reversed at next engineer availability.

Runbook integration points (where to link things)
------------------------------------------------
- platform-operator-dashboard: provide panel links for the impacted service, latency and error-rate panels, and the last deploy marker.
- incident-tracker: always create or append to an incident ID for anything outside routine thresholds (error-rate > 1% for 10m or latency P95 > 3x baseline).
- PagerDuty: update the incident with handoff notes and any temporary suppressions.

Operator fatigue & swap protocol (practical)
------------------------------------------
1. If you feel cognitive decline, signal in the bridge: "Swap requested — tired".
2. A backup operator or escalation contact should accept and perform a 5-minute sync.
3. If no backup is available within 10 minutes, mark the incident as "operator-swap-pending" and escalate to oncall lead.
4. Documentation after swap: both operators must write a 3-sentence context summary within 30 minutes.

Metrics and signals we track for continuous improvement
-----------------------------------------------------
- Handoff completeness score (manual audit metric): % of handoffs that include all template fields. Target: 95%.
- Swap frequency per operator per quarter: target < 2 emergency swaps per operator per quarter.
- Post-incident stress survey (anonymous): median score baseline and target improvement.

How managers and leads should use this playbook
----------------------------------------------
- Review a sample of handoff notes during oncall retro cycles (weekly).
- Monitor swap frequency and investigate operational causes (chronic midnight deploys, understaffing).
- Run a quarterly 1-hour "handoff role-play" gameday for new rotations.

Runbook examples and templates (text table)
------------------------------------------
The table below is a short reference you can paste into runbook templates.
Fields | Purpose | Example
-------|---------|-------
Handoff Title | Short one-line summary | kv-prefix-cache — degraded reads
Impact | Who/what is affected | internal tenants; us-west traffic 40% of requests
Immediate Action | Next step to carry forward | rollback prefetch-2 experiment
Signal Links | Dashboards & queries | panel:platform-operator-dashboard?k=kv-cache
Escalation | Who to page next | SRE Lead (Ethan Li) — Slack @ethan

Retrospectives and continuous improvement
----------------------------------------
- Capture learning: each oncall team should nominate two handoffs per month for anonymized review.
- Feed learnings into the operator-playbook repo as examples (create PRs with redacted content).
- Track whether handoff completeness correlates with time-to-restore and adjust training content.

Ownership and contact list
--------------------------
- Playbook owner: Maya Patel (eng-platform) — contact: maya@redwood.example.com
- Oncall lead: Ethan Li — contact: ethan@redwood.example.com
- Psychological safety liaison: Nadia Gomez (People Ops) — contact: nadia@redwood.example.com

Appendix A: Quick handoff script (30 seconds)
--------------------------------------------
1. State the one-line brief.
2. Say the current impact and last action.
3. State the one next step and the confidence level (high/medium/low).
4. Confirm the outgoing operator’s swap criteria and fatigue level.

Appendix B: Example Slack snippet to use after handoff
------------------------------------------------------
"Handoff: kv-prefix-cache — degraded reads; rollback prefetch-2 pending. Incident p-inc-4912. Next: rollback (manual) at 14:17 UTC if errors persist. Contact: @ethan for escalation. Full handoff note attached to p-inc-4912."
